note: Site BV014 just off PA 75 (Path Valley Road), 2.4 miles north of US 30 at Fort Loudon: a gravel and grass lot in the woods about 60 m west of the highway that DCNR says holds one camper trailer or two vehicles with tents. DCNR's own description: access is steep and a little rough, the site is slightly uneven, and it is somewhat hidden from the road but could be noisy. The 170-ft driveway is graded severe and climbs about 9 m from the highway. A stone fire ring is the only amenity listed. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: open year round, bookable (nights offered Nov 2026, May and Jul 2027), $10/$15 + $6.50, 40 ft, back-in gravel, SEVERE driveway 170 ft, site 65 x 16 ft, 20-ft clearance. Imagery rendered (leaf-off): PA 75, paved, 25 m east of the pin; a grass clearing ~40 x 20 m about 30 m west of the pin with a white vehicle on it. 3DEP: highway 229.8 m, clearing 239.4 m, about 60 m apart (16% mean). NHD: unnamed intermittent stream 75 m away. Access is the state highway itself, so no forest-road approach.
flags: DRIVEWAY, possible drop: 'Driveway Grade: Severe' with 'Access is steep and a little rough and site is slightly uneven'; 3DEP gives about 9.5 m of climb in about 60 m (16% mean) straight off PA 75, and the site is posted 16 ft wide. A 23-ft motorhome with rear overhang may ground on the entry. Kept and flagged; owner's call.

PIN LEAD (not written): the stored pin 39.94942,-77.91287 is the ReserveAmerica / DCNR GIS point, which falls between the highway and the pad. The clearing seen on imagery centres on about 39.94945,-77.91325, roughly 32 m west. Marginal against the 30 m rule.
Beside a state highway: yes, PA 75 is about 60 m from the pad and 25 m from the stored pin; DCNR says 'could be noisy'.
Equipment categories on the site page: 'RV Site, Tent Site, Trailer Site'.
Bear Valley brochure (July 2026): the one site marked 'CLOSED for Evaluation and Maintenance' is BV008 Clarks Knob (Broad Mountain Road at Clarks Knob Road), not this site.
Winter: the Buchanan camping page states no closure period. Access is from a state highway, so the unplowed forest road caveat applies only to the driveway.
